newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Steady on expected Indon demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Steady on expected Indon demand.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil and jet fuel markets were steady in a quiet trade on Monday amid anticipated demand from Indonesia ahead of a scheduled shutdown at a crude unit in Balikpapan, traders said.
They said the market has largely factored in demand for July from Indonesia which would mostly be covered by the arbitrage cargoes.
They said this would help prop up the market as more cargoes are said to be heading this way from the Mediterranean.
The 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude unit at the 265,000-bpd Balikpapan complex is scheduled to shut for one month from July 10, company source said on Monday.
The physical gas oil market was well bid with three buyers seen at between $25.10 and $25.35 per barrel for June lifting free-on-board basis. Four offers were seen at $25.30, $25.60 and $25.80.
One cargo traded at $25.35 per barrel lifting June 28-Jul 2, traders said.
Jet fuel was also well-offered with three sellers seen at $24.50, $24.80 and $25.00, straddling Friday's trade of $24.55 and $24.70 per barrel fob. But buyers were at bay.
Demand for kerosene has emerged from Nepal whose tender for July 1-10 delivery closes on Tuesday, traders said.
Swaps gas oil was also steady at $25.20/$25.30 for June with a deal seen at $25.25.
